GOLF CROQUET · 3D CLUB EDITION
WELCOME TO THE CLUB

Aim. Swing. Outplay.

  1. Aim: tap or click the lawn. The dotted line shows your chosen direction, with yard marks along the lawn. Each shot starts aimed toward your next wicket (or stake); click to change direction and fine-tune it yourself. In Shot view, the camera stays fixed while you aim; tap Shot view again to recenter. Fine-tune with the slider or ← → keys.
  2. Swing: hold the swing pad (or Space) to build power over 2.6 seconds. Release to lock power and start the accuracy marker. Tap the pad or press Space again when the marker reaches the center band to strike straight. Early or late timing adds a gentle directional error. If you miss the meter it strikes at the far end. Escape cancels the meter. Thumb movement no longer changes accuracy. Yard marks and estimated roll help judge distance; grass and shot variation still apply. Select Roll shot to try a Jump shot. Power controls height and carry; flying over a hoop does not score.
  3. Association placement: after a roquet, the mallet disappears and the view closes in overhead. Tap or drag on the side of the other ball where you want to place your ball, or adjust the position slider. Your ball stays in contact. Confirm placement to bring back the mallet; the aim starts through the other ball. Use Reposition ball to change sides before swinging.
  4. Score: send the whole ball through its highlighted hoop in the arrow direction, or hit the highlighted stake when it is next in your sequence.
  5. Keep your bearings: the clock-tower pavilion always marks the north end of the lawn.
  6. Play tactically: knock opponents away, block a hoop, or set up your second ball. A knocked-through ball scores for its owner.

Game rules

Association and Backyard support 2, 3, or 4 players with one human. Two players use the usual two-ball sides. With 3 or 4 players, this app uses a club free-for-all: one ball each, Blue (you), then Red, Black, and Yellow (computers). First player to finish their ball’s course wins; bonus-shot rules still apply. This is a custom multiplayer format.
